title: Play your own music files through Alexa with an agent
summary: Pieter Levels had Claude Code help build an Alexa skill that plays his purchased MP3s from cloud storage on voice command; he says it worked and may replace Spotify.
agent_role: Claude Code wrote the skill's code files and guided setup; the author uploaded music, built the skill in the console and added an Alexa Routine by hand.
outcome: Author reports that saying "Alexa, coffee jazz" now plays his own files, and he plans to cancel Spotify.
what_they_did: Pieter Levels put purchased jazz MP3s in a cloud storage bucket. Claude Code wrote the code for a custom Alexa skill it named Jukebox. He built it in Amazon's developer console and added a routine so a short phrase starts it.
how_it_went: He says it worked, with playlists for coffee jazz, bossa nova and lofi. New music dropped into storage plays automatically.
worth_knowing: He had to manually add an Alexa Routine so "Alexa, coffee jazz" maps to "Alexa, ask the jukebox to play coffee jazz."
prompt: Help me build a custom Alexa skill that plays my own music files. My MP3s are in [cloud storage bucket]. Organize them into playlists by folder, like [genre names]. Write the skill code, then walk me step by step through creating and testing it in the Alexa Developer Console. Explain how to set up an Alexa Routine so I can say a short phrase like "Alexa, [playlist name]". Show me the plan before writing code, and don't make any files public without asking me.

curation.rationale: A concrete, relatable home project with clear steps and a clear split between what Claude Code did and the manual setup; lightly evidenced but easy to try.
